gaps.what: No border move is explained after 625: the 732, 751 and 772 Cliopatria steps and the Gilgit/Little Palur land; the Kalhana conquests are legend or raids on every page opened
The 'Kashmir' Cliopatria row (626-1343, sa-03) is the other half of the same realm and shares no cell with these shapes; the two dossiers must be reconciled
602, 623 and 732 shape steps and the 642-655 interregnum are undated or 'unclear' on the five pages; Kalachuri/Maharashtra, Kalinga and Kosala years bridged at confidence 1
No reign years for four of the seven kings; Magadha 555-574 (Later Guptas) and the 607-611 years not verified; Jharkhand and Nepal left as drawn
Kabul Shahi state after 870 (Hindu Shahis at Udabhandapura, Lalliya 878, Punjab, to 1026) and the Yabghus of Tokharistan are not covered
Kongu (765), Venad (825) and Sri Lanka passages are reign-dated only; the victor at Kumbakonam c. 880 is not named; the end 915 differs from Cliopatria's 921
Pre-593 Gauda, the extent of the Odisha lands and the exact end year are not on the pages; the Bengal stretch back to 554 and forward to 637 is a reading
Capitals' years, rulers and the 720 Tang recognition; one source page plus the Turk Shahi page

problems: Cliopatria rows found wrong: turk-shahis 561-664 (Nezak, drawn in alchon-huns) and 870-874; karkota-dynasty 592-625 (Afghan Tokharistan, not Kashmir) and the Afghan half of 626-655; maukhari-dynasty draws Bengal, Odisha and Chhattisgarh; pandya-dynasty ends 915 on the pages, not 921.
The Cliopatria rows 'Karkota Dynasty' and 'Kashmir' (626-1343) are complementary halves of one realm (no shared cell); the kashmir dossier and karkota-dynasty must be reconciled before the compile.

Timing mismatches between dossiers: alchon-huns hands Kabul over in 670 but turk-shahis starts 665; harsha-s-empire (Cliopatria 612) should start 606 to take the Maukhari land; chola-empire should date the Pandya conquest 910-915 (pandya-dynasty ends 915, Cliopatria 921); kadamba-empire dissolves 540 but chalukya-dynasty starts 543; kalachuris-of-mahishmati dissolves 625 to Chalukya but the Chalukya Maharashtra step is 623.

Colour continuity (rule 2): hindu-shahis should continue turk-shahis; pandya-empire (sa-04, shares Wikidata Q844910) should share pandya-dynasty's family and hue; eastern-chalukyas should sit near chalukya-dynasty.
The turk-shahis dossier ends 870 although the dynasty continued at Udabhandapura as the Hindu Shahis (Cliopatria 874): a hindu-shahis dossier is needed.
Occupation events follow the Tang worked example (the owner's dossier names the occupier as counterpart); the schema text reads the other way round.
19 distinct pages were opened (sources_total 23 counts a page once per dossier that cites it). No tool failures; the 'Kabul Shahi' page is only a disambiguation page.
